source_review.notes: Reviewed the foundational McKenney-Slingwine RCU lineage, current official Linux overview, requirements, and list semantics, the current ISO C++ draft RCU clause, WG21 P2545R2, McKenney's RCU engineering text, and Herlihy-Wing linearizability. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. Linux-specific traversal/accessor claims remain attributed to Linux; the finite model and general exposition do not claim one universal RCU implementation.

evidence: Checked protected root, immutable versions, reader intervals, publication/removal/retirement events, pre-existing reader set, and grace predicate.
Checked operation linearization points are publication/unlink events while grace completion is a separate lifetime event.
Checked retire rates, grace delay, backlog bytes, coexisting versions, reader/update latency, and callback time remain empirical unless assumptions are bounded.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation distinguishes whole-version views from linked weak traversal and never models grace as abstract update effect.

evidence: Recomputed the finite trace: reader R retains V0, publication installs V1, reader N obtains V1, and V0 remains ineligible until R exits.
Recomputed final current V1, reclaimed sequence [V0], both reader views stable, and no old version access after reclamation in the trace.
Checked the 4 GiB-per-second with five-second grace example can retain multiple old versions beyond a two-version assumption.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No exact retained-byte total is asserted where callback timing, build overlap, batching, or live sharing are unspecified.

evidence: Verified private initialization plus release publication and prescribed subscription makes one immutable version safely consumable.
Verified removal closes future acquisition while grace waits only for readers capable of holding the old path before removal.
Verified concurrent writers require serialization/CAS-rebase to avoid stale-copy lost updates; RCU reader safety alone supplies no writer composition.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Linked traversal, mutable fields, pointer ownership conversion, publication ordering, writer semantics, and lifetime each retain separate proof obligations.

evidence: Reviewed empty/initial version, half publication, old/new readers, insert/delete/replace, cleared old links, weak mixed traversal, in-place key mutation, and multiple writers.
Reviewed pointer escape, nesting, self-wait, false QSBR quiescence, preemption, async migration, callback capture/reentrancy, allocation failure, and cancellation around publication.
Reviewed stalled readers, callback/byte backlog, full-copy bursts, destructors, CPU/thread lifecycle, plugin/domain unload, shutdown drainage, memory caps, and denial-of-service pressure.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Cases cover semantic consistency, memory ordering, lifetime, progress, scheduling, resource bounds, and lifecycle.

evidence: The finite model publishes only a newly initialized version, records the old version retired, and refuses reclaim while any modeled reader holds it.
Exact assertions check old/new view tuples, pre/post-exit grace predicates, old-version liveness, final root, reclamation order, and aggregate outcome.

Chapter invariants cover reader scope, nonescape, initialization/publication/subscription, complete removal paths, old traversal validity, grace, writer serialization, mutable fields, and lifecycle bounds.
invariant_checking.notes: The model's direct reader-to-version map is intentionally stronger/simpler than real quiescence tracking and exercises no linked or weak-memory behavior.

evidence: Reviewed whole-version copy/replace, structural-sharing lifetime, publication/subscription, insert/delete/replace paths, old-link preservation, and writer composition.
Reviewed grace semantics, continuous new readers, classic/preemptible/QSBR/SRCU distinctions, synchronous versus callback reclamation, pointer conversion, and snapshot limits.
Reviewed progress/memory analysis, structure choices, testing layers, alternatives, operational metrics, shutdown/unload, and all exercise solutions.
proof_review.notes: The chapter avoids universal claims about read blocking, migration, accessors, list visibility, callback drainage, or quiescence across different RCU domains.

evidence: Reader/publication, removal/grace, and abstract-correctness arguments are separate proof structures with named assumptions.
Weak traversal is labeled contract-specific and not promoted to snapshot linearizability.
The finite whole-version model, litmus tests, history checking, lifetime tools, fault tests, and benchmarks are separated by evidence scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No fast read path, atomic root, grace completion, test pass, or documentation example is generalized into complete data-structure correctness.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python version/grace model passed exact twelve-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
It emits evidence=finite_rcu_version_grace_model and reproduces old/new immutable views, blocked grace, post-exit reclamation, and current-root preservation.
All eight external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local links passed chapter validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No real threads, RCU domain, atomics/barriers, linked traversal, writer race, callback queue, arbitrary schedule, memory model, progress, retention, or performance experiment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter decomposes RCU into reader delimitation, publication/subscription, writer synchronization, and grace/reclamation, then derives whole-version and linked-structure semantics without confusing lifetime with snapshots.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed domain/flavor selection, accessors, immutable and mutable fields, writer locks/CAS, linked updates, pointer escape, QSBR/preemption/task topology, callbacks/destructors, rate/memory admission, metrics, unload/shutdown, alternatives, and rollback criteria.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet captures the four mechanisms and caveats; the finite model makes pre-existing versus new readers concrete; ten examples cover common races; five exercises progress through definition, tracing, diagnosis, design, and transfer with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, McKenney, Slingwine, Linux, WG21, ISO C++, Herlihy, Wing, operating-system, concurrency, security, performance, reliability, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither a concrete RCU implementation/domain, real atomics/accessors/barriers, linked weak traversal, mutable-field synchronization, writer composition, arbitrary schedules, callback/grace progress, QSBR/preemption/task lifecycle, bounded backlog/memory, shutdown/unload, production latency/throughput/fairness, certification, nor deployment fitness.
